boundaries.description: Westminster Parliamentary Constituencies (July 2024) Boundaries UK BGC
boundaries.notes: BGC (20m generalised, clipped) layer; simplified a further 10% with mapshaper for web payload size. 650 features, GSS-coded (PCON24CD).

composition.method: Members/Search filtered by MembershipInDateRange covering 2025-01-01; party resolved from each member's partyAffiliations history (not latestParty, which reflects today) to correctly capture defections/independence between the 2024 GE and the as-of date; majority/election date from Location/Constituency/{id}/ElectionResults, picking the most recent result on or before 2025-01-01.
composition.notes: voteShare/turnout/electorate/results now populated — see the 'results' entry below (P1.14).

results.description: Full previous-election candidate-level vote-share breakdown (every candidate, not just the winner), plus turnout and electorate, merged onto each commons seat's voteShare/turnout/electorate/results fields
results.method: For each constituency (enumerated via Location/Constituency/Search, 650 total): Location/Constituency/{id}/ElectionResults picks the most recent result on or before 2025-01-01 (same as-of-date rule as composition) to get electorate/turnout/electionId, then Location/Constituency/{id}/ElectionResult/{electionId} returns the full candidate array (name, party, votes, voteShare, rankOrder); sorted by rankOrder so results[0] is always the winner. voteShare converted from the API's 0-1 fraction to a percentage (3dp).
results.notes: P0.3.2 deliberately skipped this (only the winner's majority was fetched) because this per-result endpoint rate-limited that script's dev runs; ran at concurrency 2 with exponential backoff on 429 this time and completed cleanly (650/650, 0 failures) in one pass, though a second consecutive run shortly after did hit a 429 on the very first call — there is a real per-session/per-window rate limit on this API, budget for it on any future re-run. The Commons Library's CBP-10009 candidate CSV (a single no-rate-limit download covering all 650 seats) was evaluated as an alternative but researchbriefings.files.parliament.uk sits behind a Cloudflare managed JS challenge that blocks plain HTTP fetches, so wasn't usable from this environment. Minor/fringe candidate parties not in parties.json (e.g. Heritage Party, Trade Unionist and Socialist Coalition, Official Monster Raving Loony Party) are given an auto-slugified id rather than added to the party master list — they never hold a seat, so this only affects the tooltip's vote-share bar colour (falls back to grey) for losing candidates.

demographics.description: Constituency-level reference data (population, area, density, employment/unemployment/economic-inactivity rates), src/data/scenarios/uk-2025-01-01/demographics.commons.json, joined by regionId (PCON24 code, same as Region.id/geometryRef)
demographics.source: ONS ad-hoc releases — population/area/density: 'Population density for 2024 Westminster Parliamentary Constituencies in England and Wales, mid-2021 to mid-2024' (foi20263363); employment indicators: LI02 'Local labour market indicators by 2024 Westminster parliamentary constituency in Great Britain', January 2025 release (Oct 2023-Sep 2024 APS estimates)
demographics.notes: Both released by ONS directly on PCON24 (July 2024) boundaries, so no boundary-crosswalk modelling was needed — every figure here is 'official', not estimated. Coverage gaps, left undefined rather than guessed: population/density covers England & Wales only (575/650 regions; the source release itself doesn't cover Scotland or NI); employment indicators cover Great Britain only (631/650; one further GB row is fully confidentiality-suppressed in the source and excluded). All 18 Northern Ireland constituencies have no entry in this file at all. Fields considered but NOT fetched this pass, with reasons: medianAge (the only PCON-keyed ONS series found is on the old pre-2024 boundaries and stops at 2019 — wrong geography and 6 years stale); qualifications/NS-SeC mix (Census 2021 is published via Nomis on OA/LSOA/MSOA/LA/ward geographies, not PCON24; ONS's 'create a custom dataset' tool can re-aggregate to PCON24 but is an interactive SPA without a confirmed stable API from this environment); urbanRural (no PCON24-keyed classification found); medianHouseholdIncomeGBP (spec §4.2 expects this modelled/estimated from regional income x IMD decile — a product decision on methodology, not just a fetch, so left for a future pass).

parties.description: Party master list: names, official colours, leadership as of 2025-01-01
parties.source: Public party branding/leadership facts (well-documented, slow-changing); colours cross-checked where possible against colours returned by the Members API's election-result/candidate records
parties.notes: onPrimary is computed (not hand-authored) via WCAG 2.x relative-luminance contrast, asserted >= 4.5:1 in scripts/data/build-parties.mjs.

polling.description: Headline GB-wide voting-intention %, averaged from polls fielded late Dec 2024 / early Jan 2025
polling.source: Wikipedia: "Opinion polling for the next United Kingdom general election", citing Deltapoll/The Mirror (19-23 Dec 2024), Opinium/The Observer (18-20 Dec 2024), Deltapoll/Mail on Sunday (30 Dec 2024-3 Jan 2025), Freshwater Strategy/CityAM (4-6 Jan 2025)
polling.notes: NI parties and Plaid Cymru aren't covered by GB-wide VI polls; left out of the map (along with 'don't know'/others) rather than guessed, so polling intentionally sums to < 100.

finances.notes: Per spec §13 (resolved): pure estimates are fine, no factual basis required. Every value carries source: 'estimated'.

lords.description: House of Lords peer counts by party/group (spec §4.1 row 2, "n/a (chamber)" — stats only, no map), src/data/scenarios/uk-2025-01-01/composition.lords.json
lords.source: Reconstructed from LabourList's 20 Dec 2024 report on that month's new-peers list (which quotes the pre-announcement state of the parties: Conservative 273, Labour 187, Liberal Democrat 78, Crossbench 184, "57 from other parties and independents"), plus the usual ~25 Lords Spiritual (bishops)
lords.notes: This environment's network egress policy blocks members-api.parliament.uk and lordslibrary.parliament.uk directly, so the official State-of-the-Parties figures for the exact 2025-01-01 date could not be fetched live; this is a best-effort reconstruction, not an official as-at-date table. The pre-announcement (not post-announcement) December 2024 figures are used deliberately, since newly-announced peers take weeks to be formally introduced and would mostly not yet have been seated by 1 January 2025 — consistent with a separately-reported '~807 members as of 2025' headline total (804 here). The '57 other parties and independents' bucket is split using the smaller named groups' typical sizes for the period (DUP 6, UUP 3, Green 2, Plaid Cymru 2), with the remainder folded into the existing 'independent' party entry (non-affiliated peers, the Lord Speaker, and the one sitting Conservative-Independent peer). Modelled as one synthetic region holding one unnamed Seat per peer (group strengths only, not the full membership roll) — see scripts/data/fetch-lords-composition.mjs's header comment.

membership.notes: Best-effort figures informed by public reporting around 2025-01-01 (e.g. Reform UK's widely-reported overtaking of Conservative membership in late 2024); not independently verified from this environment, so treated as estimates throughout.
